input.message:
I applied the review fixes to all five analyses. I rejected none outright; I narrowed three (one in pan, two in tran), with reasons below. cite-check passes on the five edited files, and all five stay `status: ready` and `evidence_basis: full-text`. I did not run `rlab index` because I was told to touch no other file. **You need to run `python3 scripts/rlab.py index 2026-11-11-ai-reverse-engineering-vibe-coding`**, because tran's `main_finding` frontmatter changed and that feeds the literature matrix.

**cite-check:** the exact command you gave fails: `cite-check` needs at least one file argument (usage error, exit 2). Run with the five `analysis.md` paths it returned **OK**: mota 60, pan 88, si 84, tran 90, wu 76 citations, all to each paper's own key.

I checked every fix against the cited page in `fulltext.txt` before applying it.

## mota2026comparing (3/3 applied)
1. **§9 bullet 1:** the outlier now changes only the raw issue ranking (replacing 59 with ~165 gives ~496, above Replit's 463), not the effort ranking (1,782 and 1,774 min each exceed v0's 941). Checked on Table 3 (p. 3) and Table 6 (p. 5).
2. **§9 bullet 4:** reworded to "effort lead robust across 2 of 3 projects, driven mainly by S1874 (>half per the authors, p. 6); template origin unknown".
3. **§7 finding 3:** the S1874 ">half of effort" share is split out as [A] (p. 6).

The version was already stated (arXiv v1, 17 Aug 2026), so no change there.

## pan2026functional (4/4 applied, one narrowed)
1. **§13 RQ3 row:** maintainability 33.45% / 31.38% and resource 31.25% / 28.92% are the two weakest dimensions; security 87.40% / 85.32% (Tables 4–5, p. 6). Verified.
2. **§9 project-type bullet:** applied with corrections. The text on how the tests were built ("documented behaviors, public APIs, usage examples") is on **p. 2, not pp. 3–4**, and the paper never mentions a CLI surface. So it now reads "black-box pytest suites built from documented behaviours and public APIs (p. 2; pytest invocations, p. 3)" and names mitmproxy, Mailpile, glances and folium (p. 2). I aligned the §10 External line ("mostly libraries and CLI tools") with this; the reviewer had not flagged that line.
3. **Prompt-sensitivity bullet:** the spread is now exact: 16.23–43.86% (27.6 pp) over all 16 models, 24.37–43.86% (19.5 pp) without DeepSeek-R1. The +7.9 pp prompt effect is about 30–40% of that. Verified on p. 6.
4. **Analyst notes:** now record the source as arXiv:2602.03462v2 (30 Mar 2026, p. 1). They also note that Fig. 4's text layer shows 44.2 / 38.6 / 17.2% (p. 7). Only which of 44.2 and 38.6 belongs to which of the two post-executability categories is ambiguous.

## si2025benchmarking (6/6 applied)
1. **§7 finding 4:** "match Gemini" is now [A] (p. 6). The [V] counter-data is from Table 1 (p. 6): WebSight's Block is 55.9 vs 80.2 and Text 86.6 vs 94.6, though it is higher on CLIP, Position and Color. Design2Code-18B is close on Block (78.5).
2. **"Miss 30–40% of blocks" (§7 finding 3, §13):** the authors' wording "fail to generate 30% - 40%" is now [A] (p. 8), with an [I] note that Block-Match is area-weighted and penalises hallucinated blocks (pp. 4–5). New [V] row: HARD Block-Match ranges 56.6–75.1 (Table 3, p. 8).
3. **Validation leakage:** added as [I] in §9 and §10 (Statistical). The model was trained on 50 of the 100 annotated pages (p. 7), refit "on the same training examples" and applied to "all 484 examples" (p. 17); the human "win + tie" rates come from the same 100 pages (Table 8, p. 17). The §13 r = 0.975 row (already weak) now carries this reason.
4. **§7 finding 2:** the "most models" claim is [A] (p. 5). [V] Block-Match falls for GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus and Idefics2, so it rises for 4 of 7. Text rises for all except Idefics2 (p. 6).
5. **HARD origin (§4, §9):** reworded as "sourced from GitHub (p. 14), same filtering (p. 8); selection of GitHub pages not described".
6. **§5 Gemini 1.5:** now says it is absent from the 484-page table, cites the footnote reporting empty responses (p. 14), and notes HARD results do exist (p. 8).

I also added a source-version note: the ACL Anthology NAACL 2025 PDF, not the arXiv version.

## tran2026vibe (6/6 applied; the fetch step deliberately skipped)
1. **§10 Reproducibility:** now "provider-default sampling, no override set in evaluator code (Table 16, p. 15); seeds not reported". "Seed" appears in the paper only as database seeding in the system prompt.
2. **"One generation per model per app" (§5 and §9 bullet 4):** relabelled [I], inferred from the SE definition (p. 5) and the separate variance panel (p. 8).
3. **§13 RQ2 difficulty/integration row:** now gives n = 23 easy / 8 hard and 37 none / 7 email+Stripe (Tables 5–6, p. 6), with strength **weak**. A new §9 bullet says the subgroup cells are too small to compare.
4. **`main_finding`:** now "judge–human step agreement ranges 31.8–87.5% by evaluator model (mean 36.1% GPT-5.2 vs 86.4% Claude Sonnet 4.5)". Verified against Table 10 (p. 9).
5. **Provenance:** a Venue note under the header now says the analysed PDF is arXiv v3 (13 May 2026, p. 1), has no ACM header, and uses arXiv pages; it was not compared with the ACM version. It also records the version drift: `metadata.json` abstract says "50 public validation", the PDF abstract says "50 private validation" (p. 1).
   - **Not done:** the reviewer's "try `rlab fetch` for the ACM version". Your brief said not to switch the source PDF.
6. **§9 GPT-5.2 bullet:** hedged as speculation. It cites the $0.093 vs $1.48 per-workflow cost (p. 9) and the timeout-as-fail rule (p. 5), and says the paper does not show the mechanism.

## wu2026looks (3/3 applied)
1. **Human labels by the authors:** "We labelled 55 scenarios" (p. 13) is now noted in §6, as a new [I] bullet in §9, in §10 Internal, and in the Analyst notes.
2. **§4 page refs:** changed from (pp. 3, 9, 15) to (p. 3, p. 15). Verified: the figures are on p. 3 and in the Table 9 rows on p. 15; none are on p. 9.
3. **Self-preference:** relabelled [A], since the p. 13 text is qualitative with no numbers. §10 Internal now notes that Gemini 2.5 Pro is both judge and evaluated model, and the only check is against one other judge on 139 scenarios from 5 apps.

I also added a source-version note: the ACL Anthology EMNLP 2026 PDF, proceedings pp. 60294–60319 (p. 1).

- Two other xiao/zhou/zhu-style version-drift items (tran's ACM version, and the metadata abstract saying "public" while the PDF says "private") remain open for the orchestrator. Resolving them needs `rlab fetch` or a metadata refresh, which was outside my scope.
